6.2 — Ground Checks: No Infinite Jumps

Yesterday's jump has a problem you already met in 6.1's bug hunt: tap Space in mid-air and you fly. A jump you can spam is a jetpack. Today: one boolean, kept honest by physics — the ground check, the single most reused pattern in platformer code.

Predict First ~10 min

Here is the ground check the starter style calls for — new code, same voice as PlayerController (private fields, serialized knobs, Update work):

[SerializeField] private LayerMask groundLayer;
[SerializeField] private float groundCheckDistance = 0.2f;
private bool isGrounded;

private void Update()
{
    // Ask physics: is there ground just below my feet?
    RaycastHit2D hit = Physics2D.Raycast(
        transform.position,
        Vector2.down,
        groundCheckDistance,
        groundLayer);

    isGrounded = hit.collider != null;

    if (isPlatformer)
    {
        if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Space) && isGrounded)
        {
            rb.AddForce(Vector2.up * jumpForce, ForceMode2D.Impulse);
        }
    }
}

Predict: the raycast is a question you ask the physics engine 60 times a second — "is a ground-layer collider within 0.2 units under my center?" isGrounded is not stored anywhere else; it is re-derived every frame. Why is re-asking better than remembering (contrast with the lever's isOn, which remembers)? When is memory the right tool and when is asking?

Socratic

The jump condition is now a compound AND: key down AND grounded. In AP pseudocode that is IF (key AND grounded). Why does the order of the checks not matter to the computer here — but matter enormously if the second check were expensive (a FindWithTag)?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — the layer mask. Raycasts need a target. In the Platformer scene, select your tilemap/ground GameObjects, and in the Inspector set their Layer to a new layer named "Ground" (Add Layer... → type it, apply to all ground objects). Then drag "Ground" into the player's groundLayer field. Without the mask, the ray would hit the player's own collider — read that bug in Step 3.

Step 2 — trust but verify with a debug ray. Gizmos make the invisible question visible:

private void OnDrawGizmos()
{
    Gizmos.color = Color.green;
    Gizmos.DrawLine(transform.position,
        transform.position + Vector3.down * groundCheckDistance);
}

Scene view: a green whisker under the character. On the ground it touches tile; in the air it dangles. If your jump does not work, the whisker is the FIRST thing you look at — does it actually reach the tile? (Character center to tile top might be longer than 0.2 — that is the number you tune.)

Step 3 — the self-hit bug. Temporarily set groundLayer to "Everything". Now the ray hits the player's own collider: isGrounded is ALWAYS true and Space is a jetpack again. Layer masks are not decoration — they are how you say "I care about SOME objects." Same reason turret projectiles ignore the turret that fired them.

Bug Hunt: The flying ant

  1. Set groundCheckDistance to 2. You can jump while standing on AIR near a ledge. Where does the character "stand" — and what did you just build (a hint from 6.3 called coyote time, but broken)?
  2. Remove the groundLayer mask field entirely and pass ~0 (no mask). Which collider does the ray find first — the player's own — and what is the symptom?
  3. Jump onto a spike. Mid-hit, does isGrounded matter? Why does the death loop from 2.2 never need to know about grounded-ness?
  4. Walk off a ledge and press Space exactly 0.1 seconds after leaving the ground. Rejected! Why is this the #1 player complaint about ground checks — and what does 6.3 promise to do about it?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Check design

  1. Two feet, one check: what would break if the ray fired from the character's center while the character stands on the very EDGE of a tile? Fix: fire it from the feet — which coordinate do you adjust?
  2. Raycast vs OnCollisionStay2D with ground tag — the other classic approach. One needs a mask and a distance; the other needs a layer/tag and gives you the ground object. Which is easier for moving platforms?
  3. Hard: the jump reads "key AND grounded" — but the animation should ALSO know (jump pose vs. walk cycle). Which parameter does your Animator gain, and which line sets it?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Build the raycast ground check: mask, distance, hit.collider != null
  • Show it with a Gizmo whisker and tune the distance
  • Explain the self-hit bug and what layer masks prevent
  • Explain re-derived state vs remembered state, with an example of each
